title: Polyglot sampleapp matrix and CI smokeplan (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact working doc to standardize a minimal set of language-specific sample apps (polyglot) + the smallest CI smoke matrix we run on PRs. Goal is to reduce onboarding friction (one-liners to run) and catch obvious regressions to SDK surface area, auth flows, telemetry, and binary compatibility.

Context / constraints (notes to self):
- Keep each sample tiny: ~20–60 lines of app code, single dependency on official SDK package, and a small Dockerfile where useful.
- CI smoke must complete in <= 5 minutes on average for each language job (use slim images / cached layers).
- Tests exercise: basic auth, simple generation/embedding call, streaming (where supported), and a telemetry event.
- This doc focuses on dev-ex internal quickstarts; separate catalog will have full featured demos (conversational, retrieval, or reranking).

Priority languages (v1):
- javascript (node) — web + CLI snippet
- python — sync + asyncio example
- go — minimal http client sample
- java/kotlin — gradle example (simple main)
- dotnet (c#) — console app
- rust — tokio async example (if bindings exist)

Sample-app matrix (one-line summary per sample):
- node-http-proxy: tiny express app that forwards prompt to Redwood SDK and streams response to client. Quickstart: npm i @redwood/sdk; node index.js
- py-cli-summarize: CLI script that reads stdin, calls summarization model, prints JSON. Quickstart: pip install redwood-sdk; python summarize.py "some text"
- go-embed-demo: small binary that computes embeddings for a CSV of sentences and prints top-3 nearest. Quickstart: go run main.go
- java-hello-gen: gradle app that calls text-generation and asserts non-empty reply. Quickstart: ./gradlew run
- csharp-console: dotnet new console, AddPackage Redwood.Sdk, run with dotnet run
- rust-stream: tokio example that opens a streaming generation and prints event deltas

Minimum CI smoke plan (per-PR):
- job matrix: [node:18-slim, python:3.11, go:1.20, ubuntu-jdk-17, dotnet:7-sdk, rust:1.70]
- each job steps:
  - checkout + restore cache
  - install sdk package from current PR build artifact (see notes below)
  - run lint (optional, only if quick)
  - run sample's smoke script (script runs the sample and a single assertion)
  - collect small artifact: stdout log + exit code
- parallelize: run up to 6 jobs concurrently in CI. Fail-fast policy: do not block others, but mark PR unstable on failures.

Smoke assertions (examples):
- generation: exit 0 if reply length > 8 characters and status 200
- embeddings: compute cosine similarity between known pair and assert > 0.6
- streaming: receive at least 2 chunk events within 3s of each other
- auth: if using API key env var, assert request returns 401 when missing and 200 when present

How to use PR-built SDK packages in CI (practical trick):
- For node/python: publish a temporary artifact to CI registry (npm tarball / pip wheel) built by a prior job in the same workflow.
- For go/rust/java/dotnet: use local replace directives (go.mod replace / cargo path deps / gradle composite) pointing to checked-out repo dir or prebuilt jar/library in workspace.
- Keep this minimal — avoid full central package publish during the PR.

Developer quickstart one-liners (for README-snippets):
- Node (one-liner): API_KEY=xxx node -e "require('@redwood/sdk').generate({model:'rwd-small',prompt:'hello'})"
- Python (one-liner): API_KEY=xxx python -c "from redwood import Redwood; print(Redwood().generate('hey'))"
- Go: API_KEY=xxx go run ./examples/go-embed-demo/main.go
- Java: ./gradlew -PapiKey=$API_KEY run
- C#: API_KEY=xxx dotnet run --project examples/csharp-console
- Rust: API_KEY=xxx cargo run --example stream_demo

Telemetry & test signals to capture (minimal set):
- event: sdk.sample_app.start (tags: language, sample_id)
- event: sdk.sample_app.call (tags: model, success_bool, duration_ms)
- event: sdk.sample_app.telemetry_error (error message)
- On CI failure, upload last 2KB of logs and the telemetry event payload (redact keys).

Local developer flow (notes):
- run `./scripts/dev-build-artifacts` to produce local wheel/tarball/jar in /artifacts; then `./examples/<lang>/use-local-artifact.sh` will link and run the smoke sample.
- Provide small helper CLI: `./dev-tools/run-sample --lang python --sample py-cli-summarize --text "lorem"` — TODO: implement.

Rollout / gating for sample library:
- v1: include exactly the priority languages and only the smoke checks described. Keep the API surface exercised minimal.
- telemetry must be green for 3 consecutive runs on the integration branch before merging new instrumentation changes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide whether to include browser-based SDK samples (fast but flaky) in PR smoke or run them only nightly.
- Rust: confirm binding maturity and whether we maintain example upstream.
- Add a tiny fake-server harness to run offline gateway tests for auth edge cases.
- Create `scripts/dev-build-artifacts` and `examples/*/use-local-artifact.sh` (high priority).

Quick checklist before merging a new sample:
- [ ] sample <= 60 LOC (excluding comments)
- [ ] CI smoke passes in <= 5 minutes in isolated job
- [ ] telemetry events emitted with expected tags
- [ ] README one-liner included
- [ ] license / third-party deps reviewed

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally small and opinionated. If you want larger demos, they belong in the examples/gallery repo. The aim here is onboarding + CI safety net.

Patch ideas (followups):
- small dashboard showing per-language PR smoke success rate (weekly)
notes: Working draft; keep short, fill in helper scripts and CI templates. Prefer iterative additions rather than big first PRs.
